text:
alyssa: heads-up — hit a telemetry onboarding snag in the Node sample app. OpenTelemetry hooks aren't propagating our internal request_id into logs, and redaction middleware seems to be a no-op for the `api_key` field. sample app works fine in python though.

matt: ugh, that sucks. is this the new `sdk-telemetry` lib? node version?

alyssa: yeah, node 1.3.0 (released last week). steps to repro: clone sample-app, `npm i`, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run `npm run start` and call /generate a few times. check stdout logs — no `request_id`, and `api_key` prints in the raw request body in DEBUG level.

jen: can you paste the relevant config you used for the otel hook? we might have missed registering the log correlation shim.

alyssa: config in sample app:
```js
const { initTelemetry } = require('@redwood/sdk-telemetry');
initTelemetry({
  serviceName: 'sample-app',
  enableLogCorrelation: true,
  redactionRules: [{ field: 'api_key' }],
});
```
logs show: `DEBUG http: received body { prompt: 'hi', api_key: 'sk-xxxx' }`

sam: hmm looks like `enableLogCorrelation` toggles correlators but we forgot to attach request_id to the logger context in node. python's integration uses `contextvars` and our node path relies on `async_hooks`/pino binding — possible gap.

matt: also, redactionRules currently run in the request pipeline only for `info`+ level — a bad default. debug logs bypass it to avoid perf hits, but that's confusing for onboarding.

jen: so two bugs: (1) request_id not injected into logger context on Node async path, (2) redaction not applied to DEBUG logs by default.

alyssa: exactly. both are pretty bad for first-time users. proposal: patch node sdk to always run redaction synchronously before logging if `redactionRules` present (opt-in could be `alwaysRedact: true`) and attach a simple middleware that sets `logger.bind({ request_id })` at the start of each incoming request.

sam: 👍 agree. we should also add an e2e sample test that spawns the sample app, sends a request, and greps stdout for `request_id=` pattern and masked `api_key=***`. can reuse our CI container.

matt: will take the node-side change. i'll open a draft PR with a failing test first. linking in-progress branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/PR123 (WIP).

jen: FYI the otlp-bot flagged a trace export error yesterday in our staging cluster that might be related — `otlp-bot: export failed: field value too large` — probably unredacted secrets making traces huge.

alyssa: oof. that explains the noisy failures. can we gate export on redaction for specific sensitive fields?

sam: yes, we'll add sanitizers at the exporter boundary. small plan: (a) logger context binding middleware (matt) (b) always-run redaction for sensitive rules or `alwaysRedact` flag (matt+sam) (c) add e2e sample tests (sam) (d) add changelog note and update sample-app README for quick workaround (`export REDWOOD_DISABLE_DEBUG_LOGS=true`?)

alyssa: assigning myself to update the sample-app README with workaround and repro steps. matt/sam — ping me when PRs are up and i'll smoke test.

matt: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/456 — includes middleware + test. failing right now as expected. will iterate.

jen: i can help update the otlp exporter sanitizers in python side if needed. also we should ensure the console/hosted logs strip keys on ingestion too — double defense.

otlp-bot: noticed 3 export errors in the last 24h related to oversized attributes — filing issue: https://tracker.redwood.ai/issues/987

sam: ok i'll add CI job to run the sample-app e2e on node and python and assert redaction + reqid presence. target for fix: next sprint.

alyssa: thanks team :raised_hands: this will make onboarding much less painful.

matt: follow-up todo: open a small RFC to harmonize our telemetry defaults across SDKs (log levels, redaction defaults, request id name). i'll draft it in docs repo.

alyssa: perfect.
